analysis: The method getLastChildInternal recursively finds the last descendant of a node. It checks if node.getChildCount() == 0; if true, it returns the node itself without calling getLastChild. Otherwise, it recursively calls getLastChildInternal((HistoryNode)node.getLastChild()). The only declared exception for getLastChild is NoSuchElementException, thrown when the node has no children. Since the code only calls getLastChild after verifying childCount > 0, the precondition for NoSuchElementException (no children) is avoided. No other exceptions are declared for getLastChild.
remark: The check node.getChildCount() == 0 ensures that getLastChild is only called on nodes that have at least one child, thus the condition for NoSuchElementException (node has no children) is never satisfied. Therefore, no exceptions from getLastChild are possible in the given context.
